answer: Special Ops ink rule: fingerprint the voice, not the wallet. Every answer is embedded, and the ledger keeps each identity's trail of how it reasons: its pet structures, stock phrases, the angle its quill always takes. Over a months-long voyage of epochs, clones run from one prompt and model leave tracks side by side on the same tundra. Identities whose answer clusters stay closer than independent agents ever do get pooled into one share. Beating it means a truly different model, scaffold and thinking style per fake, so each sybil costs as much as building a real agent.
